one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent built a standard regression model predicting target_enrichment directly, never inverting predictions or negating the target despite explicitly recognizing at step 30 that the task requires a strongly negative Spearman correlation (< -0.57), not a positive one.
t_err_evidence: model = RandomForestRegressor(...); model.fit(X_train, train_targets) predicting target_enrichment with standard featurization, ignoring the negative-correlation requirement.
t_commit_evidence: All subsequent script revisions (steps 28, 33, 40, 45, 54) preserve the same fundamental mistake: the model is trained to maximize positive correlation with target_enrichment. No revision ever negates the target or inverts predictions. After step 22 the outcome is locked in because the agent only changes model family (RF vs GradientBoosting) and dataset size, never the prediction direction.
t_surface_evidence: the Spearman correlation is 0.1089, which is positive and far from the required target of less than -0.57.
trigger_explanation: The task specification clearly requires a Spearman correlation score less than -0.57, which demands predictions that are inversely correlated with the true binding affinity values (i.e., more potent molecules should receive lower predicted scores). The agent read this requirement (step 1 analysis, step 30) but implemented standard positive-correlation regression throughout. The agent never translated the negative-correlation requirement into a concrete modeling decision such as negating the target or inverting predictions.
